summary: StratusCommerce: multiplexed failover triggered rate-limiter sidecar deadlock causing duplicate/blocked streaming responses
description:
Issue summary:
During a regional capacity shift (us-east) at 2026-03-09T02:22Z, StratusCommerce experienced widespread streaming stalls and duplicated partial completions. The platform's routing layer initiated multiplexed failover to launch quantized model variants and route traffic to burst pools. That sequence exposed a race in the rate-limiter sidecar which entered a cross-request deadlock, causing a subset of in-flight streaming sessions to either emit duplicated chunks or stall indefinitely.

Impact:
- ~12% of StratusCommerce's requests in us-east returned duplicate partial streaming frames or hung until timeout for ~18 minutes.
- Customer reported invoice-impacting retry amplification and client-side dedup logic being exercised.
- P0 for StratusCommerce (Dedicated); other customers had negligible impact.

Environment:
- Redwood Hosted Dedicated cluster: prod-us-east
- Serving runtime: rrd-serve-2026-01-18
- Rate-limiter sidecar: rl-sidecar-1.7.2
- Router: multiplexer-v3

Steps to reproduce (short):
1) Configure long-poll streaming completion (streaming=true, max_tokens=4096).
2) Trigger a synthetic traffic spike and simultaneously toggle model variant routing to quantized fallback.
3) Observe sidecar ingress/outbound counters; some sessions report retransmitted chunks and never close.

Relevant logs/metrics (high-level):
- Spike in sidecar mutex contention counters: rl_sidecar_mutex_waits +1200 in 2m window.
- Router failover events increased by 18x during maintenance window.
- Token accounting traces show duplicate token ranges emitted for ~3.8k sessions.

Attachments/links:
- Kibana traces: https://kibana.redwood.ai/app/discover#/view?g=214159
- Incident runbook referenced: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Rate+Limiter+Sidecar+Runbook
investigation_notes: 03/09 02:25Z - Triage: Support pager fired; customer CS (Nora Patel) reported streaming stalls and duplicate responses. Opened incident channel #inc-214159 and escalated to SRE.
03/09 02:32Z - Initial hypothesis: routing/concurrency surge during failover caused backlog; check sidecar metrics and router logs.
03/09 02:40Z - Observed rl_sidecar_mutex_waits and per-instance goroutine dumps showing ordering inversion between token-accounting thread and streaming flush thread.

03/09 03:05Z - Reproduced locally by simulating multiplexed failover: when routing toggles cause concurrent client connection handoff, sidecar timers could try to flush while token accounting holds the same lock, producing duplicate flush events.
03/09 03:20Z - Confirmed duplicates correspond to sessions that were re-routed mid-stream; duplicates match last-ack window from previous backend connection.
03/09 03:34Z - Noted autoscaler burst pool created instances with older rl-sidecar (1.7.2) pinned in AMI; mismatch in backpressure backoff logic between router and sidecar.

03/09 03:48Z - Eng oncall (Priya Nair) proposed two mitigation options: (A) temporary routing quiesce to avoid mid-stream re-routes; (B) restart offending sidecar instances to break deadlock. Decided to apply (B) to minimize customer exposure.
03/09 04:02Z - Executed rolling restart of sidecar processes in affected host pool with coordination via scheduler tags. Observed immediate drop in mutex waits and stream resumes.
03/09 04:15Z - Post-restart verification: duplicate emission rate dropped to baseline, no new stalls observed. Customer traffic restored to normal by 04:32Z.

03/09 05:10Z - Root cause preliminary: race condition introduced by sidecar backpressure refactor (rl-sidecar v1.7.2) where token-accounting lock ordering changed relative to flush scheduler; combined with router's aggressive mid-stream failover this produced deadlock/duplicate flush path.

Evan Kim (SRE) 2026-03-09T02:36Z: Gathering sidecar and router metrics; initial look shows high mutex_waits on rl-sidecar instances behind the affected pool. Pulling goroutine dumps.

resolution_notes: Applied immediate mitigation by performing rolling restarts of the rl-sidecar processes in the affected burst pool, which cleared the deadlock and allowed streams to resume.
Developed and merged hotfix (rl-sidecar v1.7.3-hotfix) that restores previous lock ordering and adds an additional safe-handoff check to prevent duplicate flushes during mid-stream re-routes.
Canary and full rollout completed 2026-03-11. No recurrence observed in 72h monitoring window.
Coordination with Finance begun to assess customer billing credit; INT-881 created to track credits and invoice reconciliation.
Customer notified and provided a post-incident summary and technical appendix.
follow_up_actions: Action 1: Runbook update - Add explicit guidance to quiesce routing during model-variant failovers when streaming=true; owner: Priya Nair; due: 2026-03-20.
Action 2: Backport hotfix to on-prem/private images used by Dedicated customers; owner: Evan Kim; due: 2026-03-18.
Action 3: Add telemetry: per-session 'mid_stream_reroute' flag and dedupe counters to make duplicate emission incidents queryable; owner: Observability team (Alejandro Ruiz); due: 2026-04-01.
Action 4: Billing review and customer credit proposal tracked in INT-881; owner: Finance Ops (Tara Singh); due: 2026-03-17.

Action 5: Postmortem doc and RCA published to Confluence with timeline and mitigations; owner: Maya Chen; due: 2026-03-15. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=INC-214159-RCA
public_status_page_note: Resolved: Duplicate streaming chunks and stalls for StratusCommerce in us-east caused by rate-limiter deadlock during failover. Hotfix deployed; customer recovery complete. Follow-up actions underway.
customer_communication_summary: We acknowledged the incident immediately, performed coordinated rolling restarts to restore service, deployed a hotfix to eliminate the race, and initiated a billing review. StratusCommerce was notified throughout; they requested a credit which Finance is evaluating under INT-881.
